g.text: Determinism is what BUYS the latency - not a nice property alongside it
A non-deterministic engine would have to persist its state to recover, putting a write on the hot path and blowing the budget.
One thread, one core, busy-spinning
loop:
seq = bus.waitForNext(cursor) # BUSY-SPIN, not a blocking wait
event = bus.read(seq)
process(event) # match, or update order state
bus.append(outboundEvents)
cursor = seq + 1
no locks all critical-path state is touched by ONE thread. The
concurrency control is the ABSENCE of concurrency.
no context switches a switch costs 1-10 us AND evicts cache. At a 30 us
budget, one unlucky switch is a third of it.
hot cache the order books, the order index and the bus cursor
all stay resident in L1/L2 on that core.
determinism for free one thread has ONE unambiguous execution order -
which is exactly what replay needs.
Busy-spinning rather than blocking: a blocking wait means a syscall to
sleep, plus interrupt and scheduler latency to wake - 5 to 50 us of
unpredictable delay. You are trading 100% of one CPU core for the
elimination of wake-up latency. Absurd in most systems, obviously
correct here.
Forbidden in the loop - each one alone blows the budget
malloc / new
unbounded; may syscall
logging
1-10 us formatting; I/O may block
any syscall
1-2 us minimum, plus scheduler risk
a database write
150 us - 10 ms
an RPC
50 us+
GARBAGE COLLECTION
1 ms - 1 s STOP-THE-WORLD
virtual dispatch in hot loops
cache miss on the vtable
GC deserves separate emphasis, because it cannot be worked around by discipline
alone. A 1 ms pause is 33x the ENTIRE budget, and it arrives unpredictably,
landing on whichever unlucky order was being processed. So the consequences are
architectural, not stylistic: C++/Rust, OR a managed language in a strictly
allocation-free style (essentially writing C in that syntax), OR a collector with
hard pause guarantees. It is a language-selection decision, not a test criterion.
The sequencer does almost nothing - and solves three requirements at once
determinism
Once arrival order is an explicit recorded
NUMBER rather than an emergent consequence
of concurrent execution, matching becomes a
PURE FUNCTION of (book, next order).
fairness, made auditable
Price-time priority is meaningless if you
cannot say what time an order arrived. The
sequence IS the arrival time - and it is
recorded, so a dispute can be answered.
exactly-once, with no transactions
Every event has a unique sequence number, so
a consumer knows precisely what it processed.
A restarting consumer resumes at its last
sequence - no duplicates, no dedup table.
Why not Kafka, given it is exactly this concept: a produce-and-acknowledge is 1-10 ms - THREE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE over the
budget. So the design keeps Kafka's semantics (an ordered, replayable log) and reimplements them at the right speed: a
SINGLE-WRITER append into /dev/shm. Being able to say 'Kafka is conceptually correct and 1000x too slow' beats either
using it or dismissing it. And single-writer is what makes it fast AND correct: no lock, no CAS, no ordering ambiguity.
Two kinds of determinism - and interviewers probe the second
FUNCTIONAL same inputs -> same outputs
guaranteed by the sequencer plus pure matching
LATENCY the same operation takes the same TIME, run to run
guaranteed by NOTHING above - and this is what the tail requirement means
Latency determinism's enemies are all systems-level: GC pauses, cache misses, page faults, interrupt handling, CPU frequency
scaling, hyperthread contention, NUMA-remote memory. Mitigations are equally systems-level - isolcpus and IRQ affinity to keep
other work off the core, huge pages, disabled frequency scaling and C-states, hyperthreading off on trading cores.
Which is why the measurement that matters is p99.99, not the mean. A system with a 5 us mean and a 2 ms p99.99 is UNUSABLE,
because that 2 ms lands on somebody's order and costs them money. Functional determinism is correctness; latency determinism
is the product.
Four capabilities from one property
recovery without a database load a snapshot, replay the sequence. The ONLY reason it is acceptable for the hot path to
touch no disk - persistence is replaced by REPLAYABILITY.
hot standby in lockstep a standby consuming the same stream reaches byte-identical state, so promotion is instant
dispute resolution replay to sequence N and observe exactly what the engine saw and did. A legal requirement.
testing against production replay a real trading day through a new build and diff the outputs.
